standard.title: Discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.description: use play, imagination, arts knowledge, processes and/or skills to discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior arts learning assumed. Students bring informal experience with play, voice and movement from early childhood. This is their first formal encounter with arts skill-development in a school context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use play, imagination and at least one arts process or skill to discover possibilities and develop ideas across at least one arts form.

nodes.label: Exploring through play
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use play as a genuine tool for discovering musical or arts possibilities — trying things out without a fixed endpoint.
nodes.minimum_width: Engage in at least one open-ended play activity involving sound, voice or movement; identify one discovery or surprise from the play.
nodes.typical_width: Use play to explore tactile qualities, voice possibilities, movement options and rhythm patterns across multiple contexts; describe what they discovered and how it might be used in an arts work.
wider: Explore how tactile qualities of materials (rough, smooth, spikey) can be translated into sound or voice — e.g. 'This rough texture sounds like...'
Use dramatic play scenarios to generate musical or movement ideas — ask 'What would the sound of this place/character be?'
nodes.hinge_reason: If students treat arts activities as instruction-following rather than play-based exploration, they miss the imaginative generativity that underpins the descriptor. Later skill development (including improvisation and composition) depends on students being comfortable with exploratory, non-predetermined making. A class that bypasses play at Foundation arrives at composition without the habits of experimentation it requires.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly frame play as productive: 'We're going to try things and see what happens — there's no wrong answer here.' Debrief after play by asking 'What did you discover?' to help students articulate that play generates usable ideas.

success_criteria: Engages in open-ended play involving sound, voice or movement without requiring a predetermined outcome
Can name one thing they discovered or tried during play

nodes.label: Exploring voice and sound
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore their speaking and singing voices and a range of sound sources to discover ways of communicating ideas and feelings.
nodes.minimum_width: Explore at least two ways their voice can sound differently (e.g. loud/soft, high/low, smooth/rough); connect one vocal quality to an idea or feeling.
nodes.typical_width: Explore speaking voice, singing voice and vocalisation across multiple activities — responding to music through movement, improvising rhythmic clapping patterns, discovering how voice changes in response to different emotions or situations.
wider: Explore sounds from found and environmental objects alongside voice — compare how different sound sources can express similar ideas
Use a camera or recording device to capture voice explorations and listen back — identify discoveries worth keeping

response_modes.reason: Voice exploration is cumulative — the wider the range of vocal qualities students have tried, the richer their subsequent compositional and performance options. Prioritise breadth of vocal experimentation over accuracy at this stage.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Voice is the primary instrument at Foundation; building a rich repertoire of vocal possibilities now underpins singing, chanting, composition and expressive performance across all subsequent year bands.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two distinct ways their voice can sound (e.g. high/low, fast/slow, smooth/rough)
Can connect one vocal quality to an emotion or idea (e.g. 'my quiet voice sounds like someone sleeping')

nodes.label: Responding to and interpreting music
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to music they hear through movement, image-making or vocalisation, and describe one feeling or idea the music gave them.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to a piece of music and respond in one way (e.g. movement, drawing, describing a feeling); share one thing the music made them think or feel.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to diverse pieces of music through movement (scarves, gestures), visual image-making (crayons, paint) and voice; describe emotional responses and connect them to features of the music such as tempo or loudness.
wider: Compare responses to two contrasting pieces of music (e.g. fast/loud vs slow/quiet) — discuss what made them different
Use body and voice to embody a character from a story, responding to background music — change response as the music changes

response_modes.reason: Listening response is richer when students encounter a variety of music — different tempos, moods, cultural origins. Broader exposure builds the listening vocabulary that supports musical decision-making in later composition and performance.

success_criteria: Responds to music through at least one mode (movement, image, voice or words)
Can articulate one feeling or idea the music communicated

nodes.label: Developing and extending an idea
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a discovered possibility to develop a musical or arts idea — taking one thing they found through play and doing something intentional with it.
nodes.minimum_width: Take one discovery from play or exploration (a vocal quality, a rhythm, a movement) and use it deliberately in a simple arts activity.
nodes.typical_width: Use discoveries from play to develop ideas across multiple forms — improvising new movements for action songs and interpreting them visually; using a discovered rhythm pattern as the basis for a chant; taking a vocal quality and using it to represent a character.
wider: Improvise rhythmic clapping patterns and then represent them visually using shapes and lines — make explicit connections between the sound and the image
Use improvised movement to explain the steps in a process, then capture it as a photographic story with sound commentary

response_modes.reason: This node integrates play, exploration and skill development into an intentional arts act. The teaching investment is in helping students see the connection: 'You discovered that earlier — now you're using it deliberately.'

success_criteria: Takes a discovery from play and uses it deliberately in a subsequent arts activity
Can describe the connection between their earlier exploration and what they are now doing intentionally
